steps.say: Adult blockage at the pelviureteric junction has two classic causes. One is an intrinsic segment where the ureter wall cannot squeeze, so urine stalls at the junction. The other is pressure from crossing lower pole vessels, seen in thirty to fifty in a hundred cases, which kink the junction from outside.
steps.tx: **PUJ obstruction** (blockage where the renal pelvis narrows into the ureter) in adults arises from an intrinsic **aperistaltic segment** (ureteral muscle that cannot propagate a contraction wave) or extrinsic compression by **crossing lower pole accessory vessels** (extra renal arteries or veins kinking the junction, present in **30% to 50%**). Both mechanisms produce upstream hydronephrosis and need an operation that removes or bypasses the faulty segment.

vis.alt: Diagram of common sites and effects of urinary tract obstruction.
vis.caption: PUJ among common obstruction sites with upstream hydronephrosis effects. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Diuretic renography gives the surgeon the exact answer needed. After a furosemide injection, a MAG3 half time above twenty minutes confirms true obstruction. Ten to twenty minutes is equivocal, and under ten minutes identifies normal drainage through a capacious but open pelvis.
steps.tx: **Diuretic renography** (functional drainage scan with **99mTc-MAG3**, a tubular tracer) confirms obstruction when **T1/2 furosemide** washout (clearance half-time after furosemide) **exceeds 20 minutes** (twenty minutes); **10 to 20 minutes** counts as equivocal and **under 10 minutes** as normal. The test is physiological rather than anatomical, so it separates a truly obstructed junction from a dilated but freely draining pelvis.

vis.alt: Intravenous urogram showing a dilated ballooned renal pelvis with hydronephrosis.
vis.caption: IVU with ballooned pelvis and clubbed calyces upstream of PUJ obstruction. Credit: Cambridge University Press.

steps.say: The Anderson-Hynes repair remains the definitive operation. The narrowed segment is removed completely, the pelvis is trimmed, and the ureter is rejoined over a stent. Any crossing vessel is moved behind the new join. Success exceeds ninety five in a hundred cases by open, laparoscopic, or robotic routes.
steps.tx: **Anderson-Hynes pyeloplasty** (dismembered gold standard junction reconstruction) removes the narrowed ring, trims redundant pelvis, and joins spatulated ureter to pelvis over a stent, swinging any crossing vessel behind the new anastomosis. Success exceeds **95%** (ninety five in a hundred) via open, laparoscopic, or robotic-assisted approaches. Removing the diseased ring instead of patching it keeps recurrence minimal for decades.

rows: Spatulated ureter to trimmed pelvis over stent
Success above 95 percent, durable for decades

steps.say: Endopyelotomy is a smaller operation for narrow indications. Working from inside the lumen, the surgeon cuts the full thickness of the back outer wall, keeping clear of anterior vessels, and a stent holds the split open while it heals. It is best for short primary narrowings under one and a half centimetres with a well preserved kidney.
steps.tx: **Endopyelotomy** (endoscopic incision of the stenotic ring) divides the back outer wall in a full-thickness **posterolateral incision**, keeping the cut clear of anterior crossing vessels, and the split segment heals open around a temporary stent. It suits primary strictures **under 1.5 cm** (one and a half centimetres) with minimal hydronephrosis. Long, redo, or poorly functioning systems still need formal dismembered pyeloplasty.

rows: Full thickness, posterolateral, away from vessels
Primary stricture under 1.5 cm, good function
Long, redo, or poorly functioning systems

steps.say: Two older repairs keep the ureter in one piece for selected anatomy. The Fenger plasty opens the narrowing lengthwise and sews it closed crosswise, which widens the channel. The Foley Y-V repair advances a flap of pelvis into the ureter, which also corrects a ureter that joins the pelvis too high.
steps.tx: **Fenger plasty** (Heineke-Mikulicz style widening) opens the stricture longitudinally and closes it transversely to gain lumen without transection. **Foley Y-V pyeloplasty** (pelvic flap advancement) advances a V-shaped pelvic flap into the upper ureter and simultaneously corrects a **high ureteral insertion** (ureter joining the pelvis above its dependent point). Both are non-dismembered repairs reserved for secondary strictures or high insertions without crossing vessels.

rows: Longitudinal open, transverse close, gains lumen
Pelvic flap into ureter, fixes high insertion
Ureter stays in continuity, no transection

steps.say: Dietl crisis is the dramatic face of intermittent obstruction. In patients with a mobile kidney, standing lets the kidney drop and kink the junction, so the pelvis balloons until severe flank pain with nausea forces the patient to lie down. Lying flat unkinks the ureter, the pelvis drains, and the pain vanishes until the next long walk.
steps.tx: **Dietl crisis** (intermittent obstruction pain attacks) strikes walking or standing patients with movable kidneys (**nephroptosis**, abnormal renal mobility): dependency drops the kidney, kinks the junction, and overdistends the pelvis into severe flank pain with **nausea and vomiting**. Recumbency unkinks the ureter and the pain vanishes as the pelvis drains. The episodic walk provoked pattern points straight at a mobile kidney rather than a stone.

rows: Walking or standing with a mobile kidney
Severe flank pain with nausea and vomiting
Lying down unkinks the junction, pelvis drains
Ureteral stone, which lacks this postural pattern

steps.say: The Whitaker test measures obstruction with pressure instead of pictures. Saline runs into the pelvis at ten millilitres per minute while pelvic and bladder pressures are recorded together. A difference above twenty two centimetres of water proves obstruction, whatever the images suggest.
steps.tx: The **Whitaker test** (invasive perfusion pressure study) infuses saline antegrade into the renal pelvis at **10 mL/min** (ten millilitres per minute) while recording renal pelvic and bladder pressures together. A differential gradient **above 22 cmH2O** (twenty two centimetres of water) is diagnostic of obstruction. It is reserved for equivocal renography or kidneys where the drainage answer decides between reconstruction and nephrectomy.

rows: Antegrade saline at 10 mL per minute
Equivocal renography, reconstruct or remove decisions

steps.say: Function decides urgency. A blocked solitary kidney threatens the entire renal reserve, so it needs prompt drainage and repair. A kidney whose share of function slides below forty percent is losing ground and also needs prompt correction. Kidneys above that line with mild symptoms can be watched with repeat scans.
steps.tx: Symptomatic obstruction in a **solitary functioning kidney** (single kidney carrying whole renal reserve) or with **differential renal function** deteriorating **below 40%** (forty percent split function) warrants prompt decompression by stent or nephrostomy followed by definitive correction. Waiting converts a reconstructable kidney into a nephrectomy specimen, while kidneys holding above 40% with mild symptoms can be observed with serial renography.

title: Pelviureteric Junction (PUJ) Obstruction: Evaluation, Dismembered Pyeloplasty and Endourology
